text_content: when the waters rise in davao city so do the online critics following the heavy rains brought by the habagat and recent weather systems on july 24 2026 several neighborhoods across davao city once again faced rising floodwaters from mandug and tugbok down to low-lying areas like bangkal matina and talomo families had to endure another stressful night of monitoring river levels moving to higher ground or waiting for emergency teams and like clockwork as soon as photos of flooded streets flooded social media the comments section lit up with the usual outrage political potshots and online bashing where did the billions go why hasn't the city solved flooding yet it is completely understandable for affected residents to feel frustrated when water enters their homes but using these calamities to mock or tear down the city overlooks the actual science geography and non-stop work happening on the ground here is the perspective every dabawenyo and onlooker needs to hear 1 you cannot out-engineer a catch basin no politician regardless of their party and no amount of infrastructure spending can change basic topography davao city sits beside major river systems davao talomo matina lipadas bunawan and lasang flowing straight into the gulf key areas like bago gallera talomo proper ulas bangkal and matina are natural catch basins when continuous rains hit the highlands upstream millions of gallons of water naturally rush downward into these lower elevations add a high tide at the coast and the ocean acts like a giant dam preventing river mouths from discharging into the sea dikes and pumping stations can help manage overflow but they cannot stop gravity or push back the ocean 2 nature remembers its original shape parts of boulevard bucana agdao and sta ana were historically mudflats swamps and coastal wetlands humans can pave over these landscapes with roads subdivisions and concrete structures but when extreme rainfall happens water simply reclaims its natural pathways with climate change intensifying weather patterns nationwide rainfall volumes that used to happen once every few decades are now occurring multiple times a year this is a regional and global environmental challenge not an isolated municipal flaw 3 where did the funds go look at the defense systems in place critics often point to multi-billion flood control budgets as if money should make water instantly disappear but flood mitigation infrastructure isn't meant to stop rain from falling it's built to slow down water protect riverbanks and buy critical time pumping stations and retarding basins built in notorious bottlenecks like sasa and la verna to hold runoff and force water past high-tide barriers revetment walls and dikes miles of concrete dikes line the matina talomo and davao rivers to keep riverbanks from completely collapsing during sudden surges early warning and river monitoring the city disaster risk reduction and management office cdrrmo operates automated sensors and live hd monitoring cameras along all six major river channels allowing them to issue preemptive siren alarms and evacuation orders hours before water peaks 4 while keyboard warriors bash responders are out in the dark while critics type away in dry rooms hundreds of frontline responders from the cdrrmo bfp davao light urban search and rescue sar units and barangay disaster teams are out in waist-deep water executing rescue operations clearing clogged channels and moving stranded families to safety good governance in a coastal river-dense city isn't measured by the complete absence of natural calamities it's measured by preparedness quick response and zero casualties the fact that emergency teams can track upstream river swells in real-time and mobilize rescue trucks within minutes is proof of a functional disaster system bashing davao city during a flood won't lower the tide and weaponizing human suffering for online arguments won't stop the rain instead of tearing each other down let's focus on what actually keeps us safe community preparedness and cooperation when the cdrrmo issues a code red or sounds the warning siren do not wait follow evacuation protocols early look out for elderly neighbors keep your emergency kits ready and respect the responders risking their safety on the frontlines
